thread:
alex: Heads up — planned maintenance in us-west2 this Saturday 02:00–06:00 UTC. We'll do a staged NIC microcode update + GPU microcode uplift on rack cluster-43 (5 rack cohorts). Expect rolling node reboots and transient capacity reduction up to ~15% in hosted pools. Affected surfaces: hosted-api, dedicated-pool-west, private-vpc-us-west2. Plan: drain cohort -> reboot -> smoke canary (2 nodes, 30m) -> continue. Rollback if p50 latency > 250ms or error rate spikes >1.5x. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/ops/runbooks/us-west2-microcode

tanya: Ack. Can you push window to 03:00–07:00 UTC? traffic usually dips later on Sat and reduces customer impact.

alex: We can shift start to 03:00. Original reason for 02:00 was low-cost burst backfill but 03:00 is fine. I'll update ticket.

jonah: Are there any Dedicated tenants pinned to rack-43? If so we need scheduled failover with SEs. Quick list command: `./infractl tenants --rack cluster-43 --format table`

alex: good call — running the list now. Output shows two reserved tenants on racks 43a/b flagged as "pinned". @tanya please loop in SE for those customers.

infra-bot: [automation] Created maintenance ticket MNT-178888 and scheduled in calendar. Notifying oncall and reserved-tenants channel.

eva: Cost/impact question — what's the estimated effective lost-GPU-hours (for billing/costing)?

alex: Quick estimate: region has ~300 GPUs, if we see 15% transient loss that's ~45 GPUs affected. Maintenance window ~4h (warm canaries + roll) => 45 * 4h = 180 GPU-hours. Internal unit cost ~ $2/hr => ~ $360 consistent-cost equivalent. This is a rough ballpark, will refine in postmortem.

paul: Add explicit rollback triggers: (1) available capacity < 20% of baseline in the region, (2) hosted-api p50 > 300ms for 5m, (3) canary failrate > 1%. If any trigger fires, abort and restore previous microcode.

alex: Agree. Will add to runbook and automation will convert triggers -> incident page.

tanya: Customer "Synthly" has a demo on Sat 04:30 UTC. Can we carve out a carveout slot or ensure their traffic routes to eu-west as fallback? @jonah can you confirm failover route for Synthly?

jonah: Synthly is on dedicated-pool-west but has cross-region failover to eu-west1 configured. Need to validate DNS TTLs and console route policy. I'll run a quick smoke: `curl -v https://synthly-app.redwood.dev/health --resolve synthly-app.redwood.dev:443:52.19.88.10`

ops-oncall: I'll add temporary monitoring alerts for: hosted-api p50 > 250ms (5m), request error rate +0.5% (3m), and host_evictions > 2 in 10m. I'll be watching during the window. :eyes:

alex: Thanks — updated window to 03:00–07:00 UTC, added rollback triggers and Synthly carveout note. If no objections by EOD Friday we'll proceed. :thumbsup:

tanya: No objections from me. I'll ping SEs and customer success.

alex: Final note for SREs: pre-warm KV cache on target cohorts 45m before drain (`/bin/cache-seed --rack cluster-43 --duration 45m`). Also ensure scheduler backpressure policy set to `cold-shed` for short bursts (keeps p99 tail low).
